## What's new

**Built on GitHub, ready for code signing.** CryptBridge works exactly as in 0.12.0. This release is about where the exe comes from.

### Windows

- **Built by GitHub Actions** from the source in this repository, never on a private PC, with the tests running against exactly the pinned rclone. A dry run checks the whole build without publishing anything.
- **Code signing prepared:** free code signing through the SignPath Foundation is applied for. Until it is active `CryptBridge.exe` stays unsigned. Only `CryptBridge.exe` will ever be signed; the rclone and WinFsp copies stay the unchanged originals. What CryptBridge sends where, what it changes on your system and how to uninstall it: [code signing policy](https://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge/blob/main/CODE_SIGNING.md).
- New in the README: how to uninstall CryptBridge completely.
- Your settings, vaults and the app lock stay as they are. rclone stays at 1.75.2.

### Linux server

- Nothing changed. Updating the server is not needed.

## Updating

- **Windows:** quit CryptBridge (wait until no uploads are running), replace `CryptBridge.exe` with the new one and start it.
- **Server:** nothing to do.

## Downloads

- `CryptBridge.exe`: Windows 11 (64-bit), needs [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev/rel/)
- `setup.sh`: Linux server (Ubuntu / Debian)
- Backup copies (optional, see above): the four rclone ZIP files, `winfsp-2.1.25156.msi`, `rclone-LICENSE.txt`, `WinFsp-LICENSE.txt`
